value: The View > Blur whole-brain one-sample t-test revealed robust activity in the MOFC (extending slightly into vMPFC) and bilateral amygdala, along with significant activity in the right posterior superior temporal sulcus, bilateral anterior inferior temporal sulcus, and bilateral dorsal LPFC.
These data suggest that viewing peer faces recruited key neural regions involved in emotion reactivity, including MOFC/vMPFC and bilateral amygdala.
